passages.note: Authored a mandatory AI-provenance disclosure law; the operative duties are transparency and detection, not harm liability, pre-deployment safety testing, or government approval.
passages.actor_quote: SB 942, Becker. California AI Transparency Act.

rows.reasoning: Becker authored SB 942 (2023-2024), the California AI Transparency Act, which requires covered providers to make available an AI detection tool and to include manifest and latent disclosures in AI-generated content, enforced by civil penalty. A binding, penalty-backed mandate rules out the side that would "Allow AI companies to develop and deploy technology freely without government interference" or "Suggest AI safety guidelines but let companies choose whether to follow them", but a provenance-disclosure duty is not "Hold AI developers legally responsible when their systems cause harm" (the penalty attaches to non-disclosure, not to harm caused), nor "Require safety testing before AI can be used in high-stakes areas like hiring, healthcare, and policing", nor "Impose strict government approval requirements before any AI system can be deployed". The single surviving passage separates the sides but not the three rungs on the oversight side.
